title: adaptive-fidelity-swapper-and-spot-lane-prd-rough
content:
TL;DR: Propose an "adaptive fidelity swapper" that can route requests into a cheaper preemptible/spot execution lane by dynamically lowering model fidelity (shorter context, quantized variant, lower-precision model), combined with a lightweight reservation for critical microbursts. This PRD sketches how to balance latency SLOs, cost savings, and tenant isolation when opportunistically using ephemeral capacity.

Problem statement
- Many Dedicated customers have spiky workloads where most traffic is latency-insensitive or can tolerate lower fidelity occasionally. Current Dedicated offering ties capacity to fixed GPU pools and tenant reservations, which can be expensive for bursty customers.
- We lack a standardized mechanism to safely and automatically divert suitable requests to cheaper preemptible resources while preserving predictable performance for high-SLO traffic.

Goals (what success looks like)
1) Enable up to 30% unit-cost reduction on average for mixed-fidelity workloads by safely utilizing spot/preemptible lanes without violating tenant latency SLOs.
2) Provide deterministic controls for tenants to opt-in and configure fidelity-swap policies and isolation boundaries.
3) Make routing and degradation observable with fine-grained telemetry so we can detect quality regressions and roll back policies.

Non-goals
- Not an end-to-end solution for full model fallback to hosted API (that is out of scope).
- Not a replacement for Dedicated reserved capacity guarantees; this augments them.

User personas
- ML platform engineer at customer: wants cost reduction while keeping tail latency bounded for critical routes.
- Product engineer: wants predictable quality for chat endpoints but can accept lower-quality embeddings during heavy load.
- SRE at Redwood: wants clear isolation to avoid noisy neighbors when preemptible lanes reclaim capacity.

High-level design
1) Request classification pipeline (fast, in-proxy): label each request as "candidate-for-fidelity-swap" or "must-stay". Heuristics include route tags, tolerance hints in request metadata, prompt length, and customer-defined white/blacklists.
2) Fidelity profile catalog: each model published to Dedicated will have 2–4 fidelity variants (e.g., full-model fp16, quantized int8, short-context trimmed model, and distilled small model). Profiles include expected latency, cost multiplier, and quality delta (from offline evals).
3) Spot execution lane: a pool of preemptible GPUs (on-prem preemptible or cloud spot) annotated as "spot-lane-vX". Requests routed here run on lower-fidelity profiles.
4) Ephemeral reservation guard: tenants can purchase or be allocated a tiny guaranteed buffer (ephemeral credits) that can be used to temporarily keep some requests on reserved capacity during transient preemption/fallbacks.
5) Reincarnation and rollback: when preemptible capacity is reclaimed or quality monitoring detects drift, traffic is automatically routed back to reserved capacity or to a fallback profile.

Config knobs for tenants (UI + API)
- opt_in (boolean): allow this tenant to use spot lanes.
- fidelity_policy (enum / list): order of profiles allowed for swap, e.g. [fp16, int8+ctx64, distilled-small].
- max_degradation_pct (number): percent drop in eval metric allowed (e.g., 2% drop in Rouge/ROUGE-L or 0.5% drop in classification accuracy).
- tail_latency_budget_ms: maximum allowed P99 increase when using spot lane.
- ephemeral_credits (integer): credit units for guard reservations; can be purchased or allocated.

Routing algorithm (sketch)
- For each incoming request: evaluate candidate score based on route, tenant policy, and current spot-lane load. If candidate and score > threshold, attempt swap.
- Swap attempt: reserve a slot in spot-lane pool; if successful, dispatch to spot-lane variant. If not, either queue briefly (ms-scale) or fall back to reserved run.
- Preemption handling: on spot eviction signal, requests in-flight are allowed to finish (soft-drain). New swaps are stopped and routed back to reserved pools. Ephemeral credits may be burned to bridge critical routes into reserved runs for the next N seconds.

Observability and alerts
- New metrics: swapped_count, swap_success_rate, swap_latency_delta_p50/p95/p99, quality_regression_rate (per-prompt-set), ephemeral_credit_balance.
- Dashboards: per-tenant swap heatmap, cluster spot-lane occupancy, and a rollback dashboard showing escalation events.
- Alerts: auto-notify when quality_regression_rate > tenant.max_degradation_pct for >5m, or when swap_success_rate < 90% during a burst.

Safety and isolation controls
- Network/tenancy isolation: spot-lane nodes run in segregated infra segments; no cross-tenant side channels beyond standard isolation.
- Rate-limits and throttles: tenants can opt to cap percent of traffic that may be swapped (e.g., max 40% of requests).
- Fallback guarantees: always ensure that a tenant can keep a minimal critical path on reserved capacity (configurable critical routes).
- Audit logs: every swap decision recorded with reason code, quality profile used, and pre/post metrics.

Acceptance criteria / MVP
- Implementation of classification + fidelity profile registry in the control plane.
- A single spot-lane pool that can host int8 quantized variants and a distilled profile.
- Tenant-level opt-in and UI controls for max swap percent and ephemeral credits.
- Telemetry pipeline emits swap metrics and a basic dashboard.
- Safe fallback mechanism when spot-lane preemption occurs (no more than 5s extra latency to recover).

Open questions / risks
- How to quantify and compare "quality delta" across diverse workloads (chat vs. embeddings vs. rerank)? We need standard eval sets or tenant-provided checks.
- Billing model: how do ephemeral credits map to cost/chargebacks? Prepaid credits vs. post-hoc adjustments?
- Preemption semantics across on-prem vs cloud spot: differences in eviction signals may complicate a unified flow.
- Corner cases where degraded outputs cause downstream failures (e.g., hallucinations in a generator). Need guardrails like safety checks or higher gating for risky routes.

Next steps / milestones
- 2 wks: prototype the classification hook and fidelity_profile registry (control-plane PoC) (ENG-4827).
- 6 wks: basic spot-lane execution with quantized model binary and simple routing.
- 10 wks: integrate ephemeral credits ledger and tenant UI for opt-in.
- 14 wks: run a 1-week pilot with 2–3 friendly customers and collect quality telemetry.

Notes / references / quick sketches
- Slack thread: #dedicated-ops "spot-lane idea" (see pinned messages).
- Confluence: linked artifact above has initial eval matrices we can reuse.
- Example policy JSON (informational):
  {
    "opt_in": true,
    "fidelity_policy": ["fp16", "int8-ctx64", "distilled-small"],
    "max_degradation_pct": 1.5,
    "tail_latency_budget_ms": 120,
    "ephemeral_credits": 100
  }

Slack / follow-ups: assigning to Jun Park and Ana for infra feasibility, Ravi to own economics model. Liam will help with telemetry contract.

Quick appendix: rough cost math (back-of-envelope)
- baseline reserved per-token cost: $0.012/token (example).
- int8 spot lane: ~0.0065/token (45% savings).
- distilled profile: ~0.004/token but quality delta likely higher.
- if 40% of eligible traffic swaps to spot-int8 -> end-to-end unit cost drops ~18% (ignoring overheads).

This document is intentionally a rough draft; want feedback on the policy surface area, acceptable failure models, and how aggressive we can be on automated swaps without losing customer trust.
